listingTitle: Avoid JavaScript string concatenation in loops
title: Avoid JavaScript string concatenation in loops
why: Repeatedly extending an immutable string can copy a growing prefix and create avoidable temporary values.
suggestion: Collect fragments in an array and join once after the loop, or stream them directly to the consumer.
limitations: Only += on a lexically visible local with a string annotation or quoted/template-string initializer is reported inside braced loops. A binding created inside that repeating loop is not a growing accumulator; a nested loop can still repeatedly extend it.

Simple local declarations and function parameters shadow same-named strings; sibling scopes, member fields, comments, strings and regex text do not provide binding evidence. Closed-over strings remain candidates when the callback contains its own loop.

Engine rope optimizations, bounded inputs, reassignment, destructured or multi-declarator bindings and arbitrary type or control-flow facts are not resolved. Captured parameter evidence is conservative; repeated occurrences are grouped per file.
